decision.title: XPath and XQuery sweep: syntax error places, run-time closures, globals after the evaluation, fixed defaults, cyclic item types (packet )
decision.summary: Syntax errors are reported at the innermost ERROR node, context-dependent functions made at run time become a , focus-free defaults become a , and import cycles run an .

body.p: , after , , , , , , , , . No public header changed; internal: sxml_function_parameter. is_empty_without_focus, two fields of sxml_xquery_static_request, the evaluator service sxml_evaluator_make_run_time_closure with its body operations and the unlisted row sxml:run-time-closure. Glossary: run_time_closure, default_global, item_type_round. Verified as asks: the debug preset (every unit and CLI test but evaluator_stream, under ASan and UBSan), clang-tidy on the changed files, the call-cycle check, the book examples (472 match), and whole XP40, XQ40 and XT40 runs with the release drivers, case by case against HEAD.

item.p: Syntax error places ('s finding): nothing is re-parsed; tree-sitter's recovery wraps a wide region, often from the module's start, in one ERROR and marks the token it could not take with an ERROR inside it. sxml_xpath_find_error now descends, while the node is an ERROR, to the first ERROR or MISSING node it holds, so a syntax error in a string constructor's { } is reported at its place (4:44, was 1:1 or the clause's start). One path for XPath, XQuery and XSLT value templates (an attribute value template still maps through its normalized value). CLI tests xquery_string_constructor_syntax_error, xpath_string_template_syntax_error; the book shows no changed place.

Run-time closures (glossary run_time_closure; XPath 4.0, 4.5.4; F&O 4.0, 13.1.1; 's and 's open item, xqhof18, xqhof19): one closure representation for a context-dependent function made at run time, for XQuery and XSLT alike: a function item whose body operations are sxml_evaluator_run_time_closure_body_operations, whose state is the IR function of its place (retaining the unit) and whose captured values are the wrapped item, the place's expression index and, for a row that takes the caller's focus, the focus there. The machine calls the wrapped item in a CALL task made a task of the place, so sxml_dynamic_context_get_static_context and its kin read the place's module ('s per-module static context) and the kept focus follows the arguments as a static call's caller focus. Two makers: a named reference to a context-dependent native row lowers to a static call of sxml:run-time-closure with the row's function item (and the caller's focus, dropped at run time when absent), replacing 's IR closure of the module; fn:function-lookup wraps what it finds for a context-dependent row at the place of its call. So <lib/>/fn:function-lookup#2 made in a library module looks up in that module, with <lib/> as the focus.

Globals after the evaluation ('s limit; ): a function item called after its evaluation ended, or from another evaluation, got no global table and failed with INVALID_ARGUMENT when its body read a global. Entering an IR function of a unit the run has no table for now adds one with every global absent: declared globals are computed again in that run on first read (), external variables and the context value read as absent (XPDY0002). A function item does not retain its evaluation's table: a global's value can hold the item, and values must not form cycles (). Unit test xquery_prolog/function_item_reads_globals_after_evaluation.

Fixed defaults (XQuery 4.0, 5.18.3: a default "is evaluated in the same way as the initializing expression of a variable declaration" with the caller's focus; PR 2941; function-decl-40-060): a default function that reads no part of the focus becomes, through a function of arity 0, the initializer of a hidden global (glossary default_global, Q{urn:sxml:default}dN), and every call of it a read of that global, computed once per evaluation. XQuery only; XSLT's xsl:function defaults keep a call per use.

Cyclic imports of named item types (5.12.4, 5.19; qt4 issue 1520; modules-43): with an import cycle the module set first runs an item type round (glossary item_type_round): every module's namespaces and named item types only (no schema imports or records), again and again with the public types its imports gave the last time, until no more are found; a module's own reading then has the found types of its imports not read yet. A set without a cycle reads as before.

"The context node, if any" (4.30's item, map-for-key-005): sxml_function_parameter.is_empty_without_focus makes an omitted context-value parameter the empty sequence where the focus is statically absent; xpath_lower.c supplies it, src/xslt_key.c (4.30's) is to set it on fn:map-for-key's parameter.

Measured (release drivers, whole runs, case by case, no case lost): XQ40 46,154 to 46,158 passed (78 to 74 failed, 44 wrong error); XP40 32,815 unchanged (26 failed); XT40 12,268 unchanged (same cases). A fresh whole run at HEAD (2c91eaf, before this packet) found no new cluster: its failures are 's (78 XQ40, 26 XP40), the kept groups and singletons.
Not done ( stands): record-003, -005, -016 and fn-string-length-26 (the draft decides against the tests); the kept groups of and .
